headline: RFD4-Proteina couples biomolecular generation with latent reasoning and reports selected wet-lab results
summary: RFD4-Proteina is an open biomolecular design model from the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design and NVIDIA collaborators. Its authors describe a shared physics-informed latent space with recurrent refinement and optional reward-guided search for generating and ranking molecular designs. The authors report selected wet-lab results, including 12 of 18 calcium-dependent calmodulin designs below 1 µM, 89 of 288 screened phosphotriesterase designs active, and four of 67 lenacapavir-step designs forming amide above background; the best reported design converted 79% of the (S)-amine and 8.8% of the (R)-amine. These are author-reported results from selected assays, not independent reproduction or evidence of therapeutic or manufacturing impact. NVIDIA separately reports faster generation and lower peak memory than RFD3 in a 200-residue benchmark. The full manuscript and supplement were not inspected in this review.
